# Harnesses

Leo runs on four harnesses. Read only the section for the one you are on; the others describe models you cannot reach and tools you do not have.

**Which one is this?** Check, in order: `CURSOR_PLUGIN_ROOT` set means Cursor; otherwise an unprefixed `PLUGIN_ROOT` means Codex; otherwise `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` means Claude Code; if none is set and Leo's skills are named `leo-<name>` rather than `leo:<name>`, you are on OpenCode. Check the environment rather than guessing from the model you think you are.

## Claude Code

| Tier | Model | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| Opus | `opus` | high |
| Sonnet | `sonnet` | medium |
| Haiku | `haiku` | low |

| Capability | Here |
|---|---|
| Subagent spawn | spawn the named native agent; its generated frontmatter pins both model and effort |
| Tier pinning | both, fixed in the agent's own generated frontmatter — a dispatcher does not choose them per call |
| Read-only roles | native edit denial — the tool allowlist omits Write and Edit; Bash stays shell-capable, so this is not a hard sandbox |
| Worktrees | `EnterWorktree` / `ExitWorktree`, session-tracked and auto-cleaned; pair every Enter with an Exit |
| Workflow runner | the Workflow tool runs `workflows/cost-tiered-fix.js` by `scriptPath` |
| Durable progress | `TaskCreate` / `TaskUpdate` — the harness owns the list and it survives compaction, so do not hand-roll a ledger here |
| Follow-up to a live agent | `SendMessage` to the same agent, which keeps the context it already built |
| Structured question to the user | `AskUserQuestion` — multi-choice, optional multi-select |
| Visual evidence | the Browser pane (start or attach a preview, then screenshot), an attached Chrome, or the iOS Simulator control tool; some arrive only after a tool search, so an empty tool list is not proof of absence |
| Skill names | `leo:<name>` |

## Native substitutions here

| Leo | Use instead | Registered here? | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `explore` (role) | the built-in Explore agent | no | a read-only scout with the same file:line return convention ships with the harness |
| `planner` (role) | the built-in Plan agent, and plan mode | no | plan mode already produces a read-only plan and holds it at an approval gate, which a dispatched role cannot do |
| `review-lens` (role) | /code-review | no | it runs its own perspectives internally, so a separate lens role has nothing left to fan out |
| `reviewer` (role) | /code-review | no | it targets a diff, PR, branch or path and scales finding volume by effort level, and can post inline comments or apply fixes |
| `leo:visual-verification` (skill) | /run and /verify | yes, as reference | both build and drive the real app, which is the render evidence this skill exists to demand |
| `leo:worktrees` (skill) | EnterWorktree and ExitWorktree | yes, as reference | the harness tracks the worktree for the session and cleans it up, so provenance and teardown are not yours to manage here |

A row marked `no` is not installed here at all, so reaching for it fails. A row marked `yes, as reference` still ships: use the native to do the work, and read Leo's version only when you need the reasoning behind a step the native leaves to you. If a native named here is missing from this install, fall back to Leo's version and say so in the report.

## Leo skills only available here

- `leo:attach-pr` — its entire product is a side effect in Claude Code Desktop's PR-card detector, which no other harness has — the same commands would run here, succeed, and produce nothing observable.

A procedure that leans on one of these does not transfer to another harness.

## Codex

| Tier | Model | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| Opus | `gpt-5.6-sol` | high |
| Sonnet | `gpt-5.6-terra` | medium |
| Haiku | `gpt-5.6-terra` | low |

| Capability | Here |
|---|---|
| Subagent spawn | generic subagent with `roles/<role>.md` pasted in |
| Tier pinning | both, chosen per spawn: pass `model` and `reasoning_effort` explicitly; a user or `AGENTS.md` override still wins |
| Read-only roles | prompt only — a convention, never a guarantee; never route work here that depends on it |
| Worktrees | no native tool — raw `git worktree` at `.claude/worktrees/<name>` |
| Workflow runner | none — fan out by hand and keep the ledger in `<plugin-root>/scripts/state.py` |
| Durable progress | no task tool — record progress in `<plugin-root>/scripts/state.py` after every dispatch resolves |
| Follow-up to a live agent | `followup_task` to the same live agent; it retains the context it already built |
| Structured question to the user | Plan mode `request_user_input` — structured multiple choice; outside Plan mode ask in plain text and default to changing nothing |
| Visual evidence | the bundled browser plugin, else computer-use, else Playwright driven from the shell |
| Skill names | `leo:<name>` |

## Native substitutions here

None. Every Leo role and skill is registered on this harness and is the mechanism to use.

## Leo skills not available here

- `leo:attach-pr` — its entire product is a side effect in Claude Code Desktop's PR-card detector, which no other harness has — the same commands would run here, succeed, and produce nothing observable.

Everything else in the skill index is registered here, including the operational skills — `leo:resolve-ticket`, `leo:review-pr`, `leo:watch-review`. Where one of them names a capability the table above says is missing, take the fallback it documents.

## Cursor

| Tier | Model | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| Opus | `Grok 4.5` | not selectable |
| Sonnet | `Grok 4.5` | not selectable |
| Haiku | `Composer 2.5` | not selectable |

Effort here: agents are `model: inherit` and there is no reasoning-effort control, so a tier means its model alone — pick the tier's model in the UI before a batch of same-tier work.

Tier collapse here: Opus≡Sonnet (`Grok 4.5`). Moving between collapsed rungs changes which role does the work, not how much thinking it gets — so escalating across one buys nothing, and a task that needs more power has run out of rungs.

| Capability | Here |
|---|---|
| Subagent spawn | plugin agent from the generated Cursor agents directory |
| Tier pinning | neither — agents inherit the model selected in the UI, so a tier is a recommendation here and nothing more |
| Read-only roles | harness-enforced — generated `readonly: true` |
| Worktrees | no native tool — raw `git worktree` at `.claude/worktrees/<name>` |
| Workflow runner | none — fan out by hand and keep the ledger in `<plugin-root>/scripts/state.py` |
| Durable progress | no task tool — record progress in `<plugin-root>/scripts/state.py` after every dispatch resolves |
| Follow-up to a live agent | none established — re-dispatch cold with the context restated |
| Structured question to the user | none established — ask in plain text and default to changing nothing |
| Visual evidence | Browser Preview against a running dev server, else a registered Playwright server |
| Skill names | `leo:<name>` |

## Native substitutions here

None. Every Leo role and skill is registered on this harness and is the mechanism to use.

## Leo skills not available here

- `leo:attach-pr` — its entire product is a side effect in Claude Code Desktop's PR-card detector, which no other harness has — the same commands would run here, succeed, and produce nothing observable.

Everything else in the skill index is registered here, including the operational skills — `leo:resolve-ticket`, `leo:review-pr`, `leo:watch-review`. Where one of them names a capability the table above says is missing, take the fallback it documents.

## OpenCode

Provider: `openrouter`

| Tier | Model | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| Opus | `moonshotai/kimi-k3` | not selectable |
| Sonnet | `z-ai/glm-5.2` | not selectable |
| Haiku | `z-ai/glm-5.2` | not selectable |

Effort here: each registered agent always runs its pinned model at the provider's default effort, so no role downscales or upscales per dispatch.

Tier collapse here: Sonnet≡Haiku (`z-ai/glm-5.2`). Moving between collapsed rungs changes which role does the work, not how much thinking it gets — so escalating across one buys nothing, and a task that needs more power has run out of rungs.

| Capability | Here |
|---|---|
| Subagent spawn | registered agent from `agents.json`, spawned via the task tool |
| Tier pinning | model only, fixed per registered agent; effort is not settable at all |
| Read-only roles | native edit denial — generated `permission.edit: deny`, refused by OpenCode itself; Bash stays shell-capable, so this is not a hard sandbox |
| Worktrees | no native tool — raw `git worktree` at `.claude/worktrees/<name>` |
| Workflow runner | no runner — `cost-tiered-fix.js` ships in the package but nothing here executes it; fan out by hand and keep the ledger in `<plugin-root>/scripts/state.py` |
| Durable progress | no task tool — record progress in `<plugin-root>/scripts/state.py` after every dispatch resolves |
| Follow-up to a live agent | none established — re-dispatch cold with the context restated |
| Structured question to the user | native `question` tool — multi-choice, single or multi-select |
| Visual evidence | no built-in renderer — a registered Playwright server, or the Playwright CLI, and only where the project already depends on it |
| Skill names | `leo-<name>` — OpenCode has no skill namespace, so the adapter registers a renamed copy; read every `leo:<x>` here as `leo-<x>` |

## Native substitutions here

None. Every Leo role and skill is registered on this harness and is the mechanism to use.

## Leo skills not available here

- `leo:attach-pr` — its entire product is a side effect in Claude Code Desktop's PR-card detector, which no other harness has — the same commands would run here, succeed, and produce nothing observable.

Everything else in the skill index is registered here, including the operational skills — `leo:resolve-ticket`, `leo:review-pr`, `leo:watch-review`. Where one of them names a capability the table above says is missing, take the fallback it documents.
